messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] P1: Elevated 5xx + timeouts for tenant vela-edge on Dedicated cluster eu-west-2. Error rate spike started ~1765439980, 5m error rate = 27%. Paging oncall_sre and prod-sre. Docs: <https://runbooks.internal/redwood/dedicated-paging|runbook>
oncall_sre: acked. I'm jumping in — will start triage. ETA 2 mins to confirm blast radius.
elaine (SRE): I see gateway 504s and model worker 5xx upstream. CPU on the pool nodes ~98% for the last 4m. KV eviction rate high. Possible noisy tenant or inference loops.
samir (infra): checking autoscale logs — dedicated autoscaler did not spin up new nodes; looks like scale is hitting cluster-level quota. Pulling quota + provisioning logs.
marta (prod-sre): leo can you confirm customer impact? Is this affecting single tenant traffic only?
leo (customer-success): velo-Edge (customer) reporting elevated errors in their app. They see request failures and timeouts for embeddings and chat. Impacting their nightly batch jobs. Customer severity: high, they're on reserved capacity.
oncall_sre: ok, scope: traffic from tenant-token: t-vela-edge. Routing shows 92% of 5xx from that token. Non-vela tenants normal.
rajan (eng-runtime): can you paste the tail of the model worker logs for one of the saturated GPUs? Need to see OOM / CUDA errors.
elaine (SRE): pasted logs:
```
[worker-45] 2026-03-15T12:26:21Z ERROR inference: kv_cache_eviction: high_pressure true
[worker-45] 2026-03-15T12:26:22Z WARN scheduler: request-timeout token 1024ms exceeded
[worker-45] 2026-03-15T12:26:23Z ERROR runtime: failed to allocate workspace: CUDA OOM
```
oncall_sre: that matches noisy-high-memory usage from a single tenant. Could be very long prefixes or large batch sizes.
marta (prod-sre): quick mitigation options: 1) temporary token throttling on tenant, 2) route tenant to fallback hosted (if allowed), 3) increase dedicated pool (but quota delay). We should pick one ASAP.
samir (infra): quota bump may take 10-15m — not fast enough. I can try emergency manual scale on existing cluster nodes (add instance) — ETA 6-8m if capacity available.
rajan (eng-runtime): can we adjust model variant to a smaller model for that tenant via routing policy? Might reduce memory pressure immediately if customer can accept lower quality.
leo (customer-success): I can ask customer for permission to temporarily switch to lower-cap model or throttle. They prefer we route to hosted fallback rather than degrade model.
oncall_sre: do we have hosted capacity? ops-bot: current hosted pool for that model family has ~30% spare headroom in us-west-1 but eu-west-2 region limited. Cross-region fallback will add latency but reduce errors.
elaine (SRE): plan: (A) apply temporary token throttling rule: reduce max_concurrency for t-vela-edge to 2; (B) if still failing after 2m, initiate cross-region fallback to hosted in us-west-1 for that token; (C) infra to attempt emergency scale simultaneously. Execute now.
rajan (eng-runtime): applying routing change now: updating route table for token t-vela-edge -> add fallback-hosted:us-west-1. Command:
```
redwood routes update --token t-vela-edge --fallback hosted:us-west-1 --dry-run=false
```
rajan (eng-runtime): route update applied. Should take effect within ~30s.
oncall_sre: applying concurrency throttle:
```
redwood tokens update t-vela-edge --max_concurrency 2
```
oncall_sre: throttle applied. Watching metrics.
ops-bot: metric update: 5xx rate for t-vela-edge dropped from 27% -> 12% within 45s; overall cluster CPU reduced to 85%.
elaine (SRE): good signal. infra, are you able to add node?
samir (infra): provisioning new node in eu-west-2 now — instance queued. If it finishes, we can scale pool by +1. ETA ~7m.
leo (customer-success): customer confirmed they accepted fallback to hosted. They reported that their requests now succeed but latency increased ~300ms.
rajan (eng-runtime): also adjusted model variant mapping for hosted fallback to smaller quantized variant to reduce hosted cost and memory footprint.
elaine (SRE): monitoring KV eviction: now stabilized. No OOM logs after routing change. Continuing 10m watch.
marta (prod-sre): assigning handoff: if infra can't finish scale, we'll keep fallback routing for next 30m and then decide RPO. Also need post-incident to review tenant rate limits and quota headroom.
oncall_sre: customer impact summary for SEV board: tenant t-vela-edge saw 27% request failure, ~15k failed reqs over 10m. Mitigation: throttling + hosted fallback + scaled up pool attempted. Current state: stabilized, 5xx down to 1.5%, timeouts resolved.
leo (customer-success): relaying to customer: they appreciate the quick switch. Asking for post-incident RCA and action items.
ops-bot: infra update: new node provisioned and joined pool at 1765440260, autoscaler adjusted pool size +1. Cluster CPU back to 60%.
samir (infra): we're leaving the node for now to handle backlog. Will monitor for 30m then consider scale-down.
rajan (eng-runtime): follow-up: add per-tenant memory-safety limits to prevent single tenant from consuming >70% GPU mem. Filing ticket ENG-RED-845.
elaine (SRE): action items captured: 1) emergency tenant throttling playbook revisions; 2) autoscaler quota heuristics to pre-warn before hitting quotas; 3) per-tenant mem cgroup enforcement; 4) better cross-region fallback automation. Owners: marta/samir/rajan. ETA initial fixes 2 weeks.
marta (prod-sre): converting this thread to postmortem draft in #postmortems and creating internal incident doc. Severity: P1 -> downgraded to P2 at 1765440300 on stabilization.
oncall_sre: thanks everyone. final note: keep fallback in place for 30m, then revert routing and restore normal concurrency after validation. Closing primary page now. :tada:
ops-bot: automated note: incident closed by oncall_sre at 1765440350. Reminder: create postmortem within 72 hours.
